findings.title: An offline rename of a never-initialized workspace is silently replaced when its folder returns with another identity
findings.body:
The edit at registry.ts:634 now keeps `pendingInit` for a workspace whose folder is away, and registry.ts:638 sets `pendingIdentity`, so the rename lives only in the registry. `availability` adopts a folder's identity whenever the entry still has `pendingInit` and the folder's id is not registered (registry.ts:718-727). The adoption runs `Object.assign(entry, entryFromIdentity(...))`, which overwrites `name` and `color` with the folder's values (registry.ts:724), and it clears only `pendingInit`. `pendingIdentity` stays set, so the user's offline rename is gone and nothing tells them: no toast, no `different` state. Before this change, edit deleted `pendingInit` unconditionally, so this adoption could not run after an offline edit; the folder showed as `different` and the rename survived.

Failure: rename a pendingInit workspace while its drive is away, then bring back a folder at that path whose identity.json carries an id this Mac does not know. The next probe (listState, or any availability call) renames the entry to the folder's name.

Fix for this path: refuse that adoption while the entry carries the user's pending edit, by adding `&& !entry.pendingIdentity` to the condition at line 718. The entry then reports `different` and keeps the edit, as it did before this change. The comment at 719 gives the adoption's reason (an identity that arrived while unreachable wins), and it does not mention edits, so this is the only path I am changing.

findings.title: The toast suppression for an unchanged pick has no test
findings.body: The early return at line 168 is the only renderer change in this pull request, and no test reaches it. Grepping the app finds no test that asserts `folderChanged` or the `unchanged` skip. The only assertion is the flag itself (`relocate.test.ts:158`), and the dialog test mocks `onRelocated` (`workspace-dialog.test.tsx:50` and `:283`), so it never sees the context. A regression that shows the toast again, or one that hides the toast for a real move, would pass every current test. Add a provider-level test: an `ok` result with `unchanged: true` shows no toast, and a plain `ok` result still shows `folderChanged`.

findings.title: RelocateOutcome documents `unchanged`, but registry.relocate never sets it
findings.body: The `unchanged` field is declared on the registry's `RelocateOutcome` (registry.ts:188-189), which reads as a registry result. Only the wrapper sets it, at relocate.ts:44. `registry.relocate` (registry.ts:866-882) returns a plain `{ ok: true, entry }` even for the same path, and it still runs an `update` that writes preferences (registry.ts:870-876). A reader of the registry type would expect the flag from `relocate` and not get it. Move the field to the wrapper's return type in relocate.ts, or note in the comment that only `relocateWorkspace` sets it.

contracts.action: Pick the folder the workspace already points at in 'Change folder…' (same path)
contracts.before_after: Before: for the active workspace the pick ran prepareWindows, gate.close, the registry update that mirrors vaultDirectory, dropPendingCaptures, gate.commit (generation bump) and afterCommit. After: the function returns before all of those. The caller (index.ts:340-349) still runs the availability probe, refreshTitles and broadcastState. The same-path mirror write is skipped, which is safe because vaultDirectory already holds the active path: reconcile on open (registry.ts:351-353) and the mirror on every switch (registry.ts:958-962) keep them in step.
contracts.visible_effect: No unsaved-changes question, no route remount, and no 'now points' toast (workspaces-context.tsx:167-168).
contracts.failure_mode: The probe still runs after the early return, so a deleted identity.json is rewritten (registry.ts:733-742). No other failure is silent.

contracts.before_after: Before: an offline edit deleted pendingInit, so a later relocate to such a folder was refused as has-items-no-identity. After: pendingInit stays until the folder is written, and the rename stays in the registry through pendingIdentity.

input.summary: Reviewed the seven files of this part. The changes do what the PR says: the same-folder pick returns early with a flag, the renderer skips the toast for it, and an offline edit keeps pendingInit so a later move is accepted. One fix-level bug: after an offline rename of a never-initialized workspace, availability adopts a returning folder's other identity and silently overwrites the rename (registry.ts:718). findings.title: An offline rename of a never-initialized workspace is silently replaced when its folder returns with another identity
findings.body:
The edit at registry.ts:634 now keeps `pendingInit` for a workspace whose folder is away, and registry.ts:638 sets `pendingIdentity`, so the rename lives only in the registry. `availability` adopts a folder's identity whenever the entry still has `pendingInit` and the folder's id is not registered (registry.ts:718-727). The adoption runs `Object.assign(entry, entryFromIdentity(...))`, which overwrites `name` and `color` with the folder's values (registry.ts:724), and it clears only `pendingInit`. `pendingIdentity` stays set, so the user's offline rename is gone and nothing tells them: no toast, no `different` state. Before this change, edit deleted `pendingInit` unconditionally, so this adoption could not run after an offline edit; the folder showed as `different` and the rename survived.

Failure: rename a pendingInit workspace while its drive is away, then bring back a folder at that path whose identity.json carries an id this Mac does not know. The next probe (listState, or any availability call) renames the entry to the folder's name.

Fix for this path: refuse that adoption while the entry carries the user's pending edit, by adding `&& !entry.pendingIdentity` to the condition at line 718. The entry then reports `different` and keeps the edit, as it did before this change. The comment at 719 gives the adoption's reason (an identity that arrived while unreachable wins), and it does not mention edits, so this is the only path I am changing.

findings.title: The toast suppression for an unchanged pick has no test
findings.body: The early return at line 168 is the only renderer change in this pull request, and no test reaches it. Grepping the app finds no test that asserts `folderChanged` or the `unchanged` skip. The only assertion is the flag itself (`relocate.test.ts:158`), and the dialog test mocks `onRelocated` (`workspace-dialog.test.tsx:50` and `:283`), so it never sees the context. A regression that shows the toast again, or one that hides the toast for a real move, would pass every current test. Add a provider-level test: an `ok` result with `unchanged: true` shows no toast, and a plain `ok` result still shows `folderChanged`.

findings.title: RelocateOutcome documents `unchanged`, but registry.relocate never sets it
findings.body: The `unchanged` field is declared on the registry's `RelocateOutcome` (registry.ts:188-189), which reads as a registry result. Only the wrapper sets it, at relocate.ts:44. `registry.relocate` (registry.ts:866-882) returns a plain `{ ok: true, entry }` even for the same path, and it still runs an `update` that writes preferences (registry.ts:870-876). A reader of the registry type would expect the flag from `relocate` and not get it. Move the field to the wrapper's return type in relocate.ts, or note in the comment that only `relocateWorkspace` sets it.
